t.E551.agn: In 2018, EFSA saw no adverse effects in the available studies; however, it noted that the EU specification did not exclude particles in the nano size range and that, due to data limitations, it could not confirm the ADI 'not specified'. In its 2024 follow-up assessment it used a margin of exposure (MOE) approach instead of an ADI and concluded that there was no safety concern at the reported uses for all age groups, including infants below 16 weeks of age.
t.E551.body: Silicon dioxide is poorly absorbed from the digestive tract.
t.E551.found.0: Powdered foods and seasonings (up to 30,000 mg/kg in seasonings)
t.E551.found.2: Foods in tablet form, table-top sweeteners and food supplements
t.E551.found.4: Dry cereal products for infants and young children (up to 2,000 mg/kg)
t.E551.prod: It is a chemically produced silicate.
t.E551.regx.0: Re-evaluated; in 2024, no safety concern at the reported uses for all age groups (MOE approach).
t.E551.regx.1: The ADI 'not specified' could not be confirmed due to data limitations; a change to the specification was recommended.
t.E551.summary: Silicon dioxide, also known as silica. It prevents caking of ground spices, salt, coffee creamer and powdered drinks.
t.E551.what: It is synthetic amorphous silica that prevents caking of powdered foods.
